newsitem.title: CHINA: China lashes listed firms making false statements.
newsitem.headline: China lashes listed firms making false statements.

text.p: Some Chinese listed firms have issued false statements on their performance and cheated investors, the Shanghai Securities News said on Monday.
One of the most serious incidents involved China Sichuan International Cooperation Co, which announced a net loss of 0.77 yuan per share in its interim results, it said.

The company announced the loss on August 23 but said in May that it would offer a generous four-for-10 bonus issue for all shareholders as 1996 interim returns, giving investors the impression it was performing strongly and attracting a large number of new investors, the paper said.
The firm, whose main business is foreign construction projects, said in the interim report the first-half loss was mainly due to a 79 million yuan loss in a project in Uganda.
The project started in January 1994 and the firm should have known earlier that it would make a loss, the paper said.

Instead of making public the bleak prospects, the firm in April issued an extra 13 million shares in a rights issue to domestic investors who then suffered heavy losses after the shares fell sharply on the interim loss report, it said.
"Such a case has caused a crisis of confidence in company information releases," the paper said in a commentary. "There are reasons for investors to lose confidence," it added.
A China Sichuan International official declined to comment.
The paper said another prominent case was that of Shengli Oil Field Daming Group Co, an oil exploration company.

The paper said the firm, in collaboration with a few middlemen including China Securities, one of China's biggest brokerages, deliberately covered up an illegal share consolidation, which resulted in fewer shares in the firm, with the aim of gaining approval for the company to list shares in June this year.
Although the firm was punished by the authorities, the negative impact of the case is far from over, the paper said.
In its Sunday edition, the paper urged the authorities to investigate what it called "deception in new share issues".
"Some companies have in their prospectus purposefully exaggerated profit prospects, misleading investors," it said.
"This should attract the attention of the securities authorities."
Among these companies was Nanjing Chemical Fibre Co 600889.SS, which makes fibres for the textile industry, it said.

The firm predicted earnings per share of 0.35 yuan for 1996 but its interim results showed only 0.008 yuan in the first half, 2.2 percent of the target. Other firms included Songliao Automobile Co, the paper said.
